title: What you grade
summary: You can grade how many tips, or when the first tip came. Those are different lessons.

cards.text:
A count grade only sees how many tips.
The clock disappears.

A first-tip grade only sees when.
Extra tips are not the point.

question.prompt: You care who tipped first. Which grade fits?
question.why: A count gives every single tip the same score.
question.simpler: Match the grade to the message you wanted.

question.prompt: Two trainings with the same score learned the same code.
question.why: The score is about labels. The code is about what the tips were asked to be.
question.simpler: Say which statistic the grade read.

recall.question: Does a count grade see when the tip happened?
recall.answer: No. It only sees how many.

deeper.note: Mostafa trained networks on the time of a single tip, so the nets stayed sparse. snnTorch also offers a rate grade, ce_rate_loss, which only sees counts.

paper.title: Supervised Learning Based on Temporal Coding in Spiking Neural Networks

paper.section: The opening argument for grading spike times.

terms.plain: grade the count or the time
terms.definition: The choice of which statistic of the spike train the training objective actually reads.
